input.quote: each Party shall have the right to exploit, including license, the Joint Program Technology, without a duty of accounting or any obligation to seek consent from the other Party to exploit such Joint Program Technology. To the extent necessary to effect the foregoing in a country other than the United States, each Party grants to the other Party a nonexclusive, irrevocable, perpetual, fully-paid, worldwide license, with the right to grant sublicenses, under the granting Party's interest in Joint Program Technology, for any and all purposes
input.rationale: The IP architecture protects Sanofi and creates no prohibited transfer to RevMed. Section 10.1(a) requires each Party to obtain assignment of Program Inventions from its own Third Parties to that Party (and Section 3.4 requires subcontractor assignment, or failing that an irrevocable, perpetual, fully-paid, exclusive, royalty-free worldwide licence with sublicensing rights to the engaging Party), so work generated for Sanofi vests in Sanofi; "Sanofi Sole Program Know-How"/"Sanofi Sole Program Patents" (1.109-1.110) confirm Sanofi solely owns its own Program Inventions and Section 10.4(c) gives Sanofi sole enforcement of them. Joint Program Technology is jointly owned but each Party may exploit and license it with no duty of accounting and no consent, backed by a perpetual, irrevocable, fully-paid, worldwide, sublicensable cross-licence — i.e. joint ownership with an unrestricted right to exploit, which sits at the fallback rather than the "no joint ownership" preferred position and is therefore acceptable. Sanofi's data and regulatory position are preserved and enhanced: RevMed assigns all Regulatory Approvals (INDs/NDAs) to Sanofi (6.2), transfers the global safety database at its own cost (6.5), and Sanofi owns all Product Marks and domain names (10.5). There is no assignment of Sanofi background IP or Sanofi Sole Program Technology to RevMed: Section 3.2 is only a narrow non-exclusive, royalty-free sublicence back of RevMed's own licensed technology solely to let RevMed perform its obligations, and Section 3.6 negates implied licences. The Article XII reversion is a bargained-for, licence-based unwind limited to Termination Products, triggered largely by Sanofi's own convenience/change-of-control election or Sanofi default, and carries post-termination royalties payable to Sanofi (12.3(c)(ii)C). Noted but not flagged: the ownership allocation in 10.1(a) is redacted [***], so the sole/joint split is inferred from the defined terms; if the unredacted text allocated Sanofi-generated inventions to RevMed we would revisit.
